topic: Reflection of Light in Plane and Curved Mirrors
key_concepts: Light travels in straight lines and forms shadows when blocked by opaque objects
The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal line are used to describe reflection
When light strikes along the normal line, the angle of incidence and reflection is zero
A plane mirror forms an upright, virtual image that is the same size as the object
The image distance behind a plane mirror equals the object distance in front of it
Ray diagrams use at least two intersecting reflected rays to locate an image
A convex mirror forms an upright, virtual image that is smaller than the object
A concave mirror forms images that vary depending on the object's distance from the mirror
Smooth surfaces produce clearer reflected images than rough surfaces
A mirror about half a person's height is enough to see the full body image
Curved mirrors have practical uses such as dental mirrors and store security mirrors
